Isaiah Berlin: Call him “the founder of modern liberalism”

source: 功利主义：继承自边沁的“最大多数人的最大幸福”原则
英国经验主义传统：延续洛克、休谟的思想
浪漫主义与德国理想主义的影响：特别是在情感与人性方面吸收了柯勒律治（Coleridge）和歌德等人的思想
他批评边沁的功利主义过于量化与机械化，忽视人类精神、道德与个性，主张一种“质的功利主义”，区分高等与低等的快乐
text: Utilitarianism: inherited from Bentham's principle of "the greatest happiness for the greatest number"
British empiricist tradition: continuing the ideas of Locke and Hume
The influence of romanticism and German idealism: especially the absorption of ideas from Coleridge and Goethe in terms of emotion and human nature.

He criticized Bentham's utilitarianism for being too quantitative and mechanistic, ignoring human spirit, morality and personality, and advocating a "qualitative utilitarianism" that distinguished between higher and lower pleasures.

source: 哲学与伦理学：密尔的“质的功利主义”使功利主义从简单的快乐计算提升为关注人格与文化发展的伦理体系
政治思想：他是自由主义政治哲学的核心人物，影响了后来的自由主义理论家（如以赛亚·柏林、罗尔斯等）
社会运动：作为《妇女的从属地位》作者，他被认为是近代女性主义的先驱之一

text: Philosophy and ethics: Mill's "qualitative utilitarianism" elevated utilitarianism from a simple calculation of happiness to an ethical system that focuses on the development of personality and culture
Political thought: He is a core figure in liberal political philosophy and influenced later liberal theorists (such as Isaiah Berlin, Rawls, etc.)
Social movement: As the author of "The Subjection of Women", he is considered one of the pioneers of modern feminism
Education and public ethics: His spirit of freedom and rationality profoundly influenced the values of modern democratic society

text: Normative semantics: The meaning of language is determined by the role of reasoning. Understanding language means understanding its role in reasoning.
Speech act theory: Language not only transmits information, but also participates in social normative practices
Social practice philosophy: mind and language are embedded in social interaction and normative frameworks, emphasizing the shaping of meaning by community
Logic and Cognition: Logical analysis tools are used to understand language, thinking and cognitive structures
Rationality and commitment: individual cognition and language understanding depend on social norms and rational commitment

text: British philosopher and theorist, an important figure in contemporary continental philosophy, radical philosophy of technology and accelerationism
His thoughts integrate Deleuze/Guattari's post-structuralism and technological philosophy, and he is regarded as the founder of "philosophical accelerationism"

source: 哲学加速主义：主张技术、资本与社会动力的加速发展，批判传统政治与社会秩序
去主体化与非人中心哲学：强调社会、技术和资本系统超越人类意志的自主动力
资本与技术批判：分析现代资本与技术如何塑造人类行为与社会结构
反传统伦理与道德批判：拒绝传统道德体系，借鉴尼采权力意志哲学，强调非规范性思维
后结构主义哲学方法：使用跨学科文本分析、文化批判和概念重构方法探索社会动力
text: Philosophical accelerationism: advocates the accelerated development of technology, capital and social power, and criticizes traditional politics and social order
Desubjectification and non-anthropocentric philosophy: emphasizing the autonomous dynamics of social, technological and capital systems beyond human will
Critique of Capital and Technology: Analysis of how modern capital and technology shape human behavior and social structure
Anti-traditional ethics and moral criticism: reject the traditional moral system, draw on Nietzsche’s philosophy of will to power, and emphasize non-normative thinking
Poststructuralist philosophical approaches: exploring social dynamics using interdisciplinary textual analysis, cultural critique, and conceptual reconstruction methods

source: 《超越人类中心主义》

认知心理学：强调人的思维、感知、记忆、注意、问题解决、语言与决策等认知过程的重要性，将心理学视为一门科学信息加工学科，借鉴计算机模型来理解人类心智
text: Swiss psychologist, philosopher and epistemologist
Developmental psychology, epistemological constructivism, important theoretical sources in the early days of cognitive psychology

Cognitive psychology: Emphasizes the importance of human cognitive processes such as thinking, perception, memory, attention, problem solving, language and decision-making. It regards psychology as a scientific information processing discipline and draws on computer models to understand the human mind.

source: 认知发展阶段论：提出儿童认知发展分为四个阶段——感知运动阶段、前运算阶段、具体运算阶段和形式运算阶段，每一阶段具有特定的逻辑结构
建构主义：知识是个体在与环境相互作用中主动建构的，而非被动接受
同化与顺应：认知发展是通过同化新经验与调整原有结构（顺应）之间的平衡实现的
发生认识论：试图用心理学与生物学方法解释知识的形成过程
text: Cognitive development stage theory: It is proposed that children's cognitive development is divided into four stages - sensorimotor stage, pre-operational stage, concrete operation stage and formal operation stage. Each stage has a specific logical structure.
Constructivism: Knowledge is actively constructed by individuals in their interaction with the environment, rather than passively accepted
Assimilation and accommodation: Cognitive development occurs through a balance between assimilating new experiences and adjusting original structures (accommodation)
Genetic epistemology: attempts to explain the formation of knowledge using psychological and biological methods

source: 《发生认识论导论》
text: "Introduction to Genetic Epistemology"

source: 被誉为“儿童认知发展的哥白尼”，开创了认知发展研究的科学化路径
text: Known as the "Copernicus of children's cognitive development", he pioneered a scientific approach to cognitive development research.

source: 受康德认识论启发，认为知识不是被动接受的，而是主动建构的
吸收生物学适应理论与达尔文的进化思想，用以解释认知发展的阶段性

text: Inspired by Kant's epistemology, it is believed that knowledge is not passively received, but actively constructed
Absorb biological adaptation theory and Darwin’s evolutionary ideas to explain the stages of cognitive development.
Influenced by Gestalt psychology and logic philosophy, it emphasizes the self-organization and staged development of cognitive structures

Layed the theoretical foundation of "child-centered education" and "active learning"
Influenced later cognitive psychologists such as Jerome Bruner and Lev Vygotsky

text: Hierarchy of needs theory: It proposes that human motivation is divided into five levels from low to high - physiological needs, safety needs, belonging and love needs, esteem needs, and self-actualization needs.
Self-actualization: the highest level of psychological needs, which refers to people’s pursuit of self-potential realization and the full development of creativity.
Peak experience: a transcendent psychological state that people experience in the process of self-realization

Humanistic education and organizational theory: advocates that education and management should promote individual growth and creative development rather than being purely control- or efficiency-oriented

text: Ancient Greek philosopher, an important representative of skeptical philosophy, especially the revivalist of the **Pyrrhon School**
He is known for his systematic approach to skepticism and the Ten Tropes

source: 十种怀疑论（Ten Tropes）：提出十类怀疑理由，用以质疑感官、经验和逻辑判断
不可知论：认为人类无法获得绝对真理，对一切信念应保持悬置（epoché）
生活实践中的悬置：通过不做最终判断达到心灵平静（ataraxia）
伦理与心理平衡：怀疑主义不仅是认知方法，也是一种达到内心宁静的生活方式
哲学方法论：系统化怀疑、逻辑分析与心理实践相结合，强调理性探讨与精神平衡
text: Ten Tropes: Put forward ten types of reasons for doubt to question sensory, experience and logical judgments
Agnosticism: the belief that humans cannot obtain absolute truth and that all beliefs should be suspended (epoché)
Suspension in life practice: Achieving peace of mind (ataraxia) by not making final judgments
Ethics and psychological balance: Skepticism is not only a cognitive method, but also a way of life to achieve inner peace
Philosophical methodology: Combining systematic doubt, logical analysis and psychological practice, emphasizing rational discussion and spiritual balance

source: 《十种怀疑论》

His research spans ontology, set theory, political philosophy, philosophy of art and love
He is committed to using mathematical concepts to reconstruct ontology and closely integrating philosophy with political practice.
He redefined the relationship between events, subjects and truth, making philosophy and social practice interconnected

source: 事件哲学：事件打破现有秩序，创造新的可能性，个体通过事件选择与承诺实现主体性
存在论与数学化：将存在论基础置于集合论，区分“存在-多样性”和“事件-统一性”
政治主体与激进变革：强调革命事件中的主体能动性，提倡通过事件和忠诚构建政治变革
四大真理程序：哲学、政治、艺术与爱情被视为人类追求真理的四种实践方式
反对现存秩序的妥协：批判现代资本主义与功利主义社会，强调激进的伦理与政治行动
text: Event philosophy: Events break the existing order and create new possibilities. Individuals realize subjectivity through event selection and commitment.
Ontology and mathematization: Put the ontological foundation in set theory and distinguish between "existence-diversity" and "event-unity"
Political subject and radical change: emphasizing the subject's initiative in revolutionary events and advocating the construction of political change through events and loyalty
The four truth procedures: philosophy, politics, art and love are regarded as the four practical ways for human beings to pursue truth.
Compromise against the existing order: Criticism of modern capitalism and utilitarian society, emphasizing radical ethical and political action

source: 《存在与事件》
text: "Being and Event"

source: 绵延 (Durée)：柏格森最核心的概念。他区分了两种时间：科学时间（时钟时间，被空间化、可分割、可测量的“死”时间）和绵延（真实时间，这是我们内心直接体验到的、活生生的时间。它是一种连续不断的、不可分割的意识流动，就像旋律一样。在“绵延”中，过去、现在和未来是相互渗透、共同成长的。他认为，只有通过“绵延”才能理解自由意志）。
直觉 (Intuition)：理智擅长分析和处理“死的”物质世界，它倾向于将流动的事物“凝固”和“空间化”以便理解。然而，要把握“绵延”和生命的流动性，我们必须依赖另一种认识方式——直觉。直觉是一种智力上的共鸣，它使我们能够“进入”事物的内部，直接体验其独特、流动的本质。他试图用“直觉”方法来把握“实在”的流动性，以此对抗当时盛行的机械论和实证主义。
生命冲力 (Élan Vital)：在《创造进化论》中，柏格森提出了“生命冲力”的概念来解释生物进化。他反对达尔文主义的机械论（认为进化纯粹是偶然突变和自然选择的结果），也反对拉马克的目的论。他认为，进化是由一个强大的、贯穿所有生命的“生命冲力”驱动的。这个冲力是创造性的、不可预测的，它在适应环境的过程中不断分化，创造出越来越复杂和新颖的生命形式。
开放与封闭 (The Open and the Closed)：封闭的道德/宗教： 源于社会压力和群体本能。它是一种静态的、僵化的体系，旨在维持社会秩序（如部落的戒律）。开放的道德/宗教： 源于“生命冲力”和神秘主义的直觉。它是一种动态的、普世的爱，代表人物是那些伟大的圣贤和神秘主义者，他们推动人类精神向前发展。
text: Durée: Bergson’s most central concept. He distinguished two kinds of time: scientific time (clock time, "dead" time that is spatialized, divisible, and measurable) and duration (real time, which is the living time that we directly experience in our hearts. It is a continuous and indivisible flow of consciousness, just like a melody. In "duration", the past, present, and future are interpenetrated and grow together. He believes that only through "duration" can free will be understood).

Intuition: Reason is good at analyzing and processing the "dead" material world. It tends to "solidify" and "spatialize" flowing things for understanding. However, to grasp “duration” and the fluidity of life, we must rely on another way of knowing—intuition. Intuition is an intellectual resonance that allows us to “get inside” something and directly experience its unique, flowing nature. He tried to use "intuitive" methods to grasp the fluidity of "reality" in order to combat the prevailing mechanism and positivism at the time.

Vital force (Élan Vital): In The Evolution of Creation, Bergson proposed the concept of “vital force” to explain biological evolution. He opposed the mechanistic theory of Darwinism (which believed that evolution was purely the result of accidental mutations and natural selection) and the teleology of Lamarck. He believes that evolution is driven by a powerful "life impulse" that runs through all life. This impulse is creative and unpredictable, constantly diverging as it adapts to its environment, creating increasingly complex and novel life forms.

The Open and the Closed: Closed morality/religion: stems from social pressure and herd instinct. It is a static, rigid system designed to maintain social order (such as tribal precepts). Open Morality/Religion: Intuition stemming from the "life force" and mysticism. It is a dynamic, universal love represented by the great sages and mystics who moved the human spirit forward.

source: 德国哲学家、新康德主义马堡学派的创始人
他以严密的逻辑方法、对康德《纯粹理性批判》的严格重读而闻名，对德国大学哲学产生深远影响
新康德主义背景1：19 世纪中叶的德国思想界在经历了黑格尔哲学的高峰后逐渐陷入低潮。黑格尔的庞大体系被认为过于形而上、过度推演，缺乏可验证性。于是，学界开始反思：哲学是否应该摆脱宏大形而上体系，回到更扎实、严格、可批判的基础？康德的批判哲学——尤其“认识的条件是什么”——于是变成重新出发的方向。
新康德主义背景2：19 世纪的科学革命（牛顿力学巩固、化学与生物学发展、达尔文进化论1859年发表）让人们意识到：科学方法非常成功、哲学需要能解释科学为何可能、哲学不应空谈“绝对精神”，而应理解科学知识的基础，这直接促成了所谓的 “回到康德”运动。
新康德主义背景3：实证主义的兴起，哲学地位受到挑战。孔德（Comte）的实证主义认为只有经验科学才有知识地位，哲学逐渐沦为“无用”。这使许多哲学家担忧：哲学是否将被科学吞没？新康德主义于是试图证明：哲学仍然必不可少，因为科学的前提、范畴、方法本身需要哲学来批判与奠基。
新康德主义背景4：19 世纪后期欧洲进入工业化、技术化、商品化时代，传统价值观受到冲击。在这种文化危机中，马堡学派与西南学派分别从不同方向回应：马堡学派（科恩、纳托尔普）：强调科学理性与知识体系的逻辑结构；西南学派（文德尔班、李克特）：强调文化与价值的哲学基础。
马堡学派：是“科学哲学”方向的康德主义，强调 纯粹理性、数学、逻辑建构
text: German philosopher and founder of the Marburg School of Neo-Kantism
He is famous for his rigorous logical methods and rigorous re-reading of Kant's "Critique of Pure Reason", which has had a profound influence on German university philosophy.

Background of Neo-Kantianism 1: The German intellectual community in the mid-19th century gradually fell into a low ebb after experiencing the peak of Hegelian philosophy. Hegel's huge system was considered too metaphysical, over-deductive, and lacked verifiability. As a result, the academic community began to reflect: Should philosophy get rid of grand metaphysical systems and return to a more solid, rigorous, and criticizable foundation? Kant's critical philosophy - especially "what are the conditions of cognition" - then became the direction to start again.

Neo-Kantian background 2: The scientific revolution of the 19th century (the consolidation of Newtonian mechanics, the development of chemistry and biology, and the publication of Darwin's theory of evolution in 1859) made people realize that the scientific method is very successful, philosophy needs to be able to explain why science is possible, and philosophy should not talk about "absolute spirit" but should understand the basis of scientific knowledge. This directly contributed to the so-called "Return to Kant" movement.

Neo-Kantian background 3: The rise of positivism, and the status of philosophy is challenged. Comte's positivism believed that only empirical science had the status of knowledge, and philosophy gradually became "useless". This worries many philosophers: Will philosophy be swallowed up by science? Neo-Kantianism then tries to prove that philosophy is still indispensable because the premises, categories, and methods of science themselves need philosophy to criticize and establish.

Neo-Kantian background 4: In the late 19th century, Europe entered the era of industrialization, technology, and commercialization, and traditional values were impacted. In this cultural crisis, the Marburg School and the Southwest School responded from different directions: the Marburg School (Cohen, Nuttallp): emphasized scientific rationality and the logical structure of the knowledge system; the Southwest School (Wendelban, Likert): emphasized the philosophical foundation of culture and value.
Marburg School: Kantianism in the direction of "philosophy of science", emphasizing pure reason, mathematics, and logical construction

Transcendence (Transzendenz): People cannot fully understand themselves through science. Existence always points to "transcendence". God is not an object, but the horizon of existence. Unlike Sartre, he denies God, but believes that God is an "unobjectifiable transcendent."

The function of philosophy: Awakening - Philosophy is not to establish a system, but to awaken individuals and make people aware of their own freedom and responsibility, which is obviously inherited from Kierkegaard

格式塔心理学核心关注：知觉整体性、心理结构与整体规律
格式塔心理学产生背景：19世纪末到20世纪初的科学革命，整个欧洲学界正在从传统哲学式心理学转向 以实验为基础的科学心理学，但是主导心理学界的“元素主义”遇到了严重瓶颈。
元素主义：一切心理活动都可以分解成最小的“元素”（类似化学元素），知觉 = 感觉元素的简单加和，心理学试图像自然科学一样，通过“拆分、分解”理解心灵。产生问题：很多心理现象根本无法通过“把它拆成更小部分”来解释。
格式塔心理学核心观点：在针对“整体无法由部分之和解释”问题反思的基础上，提出“整体大于部分之和”
诞生时心理学界的主流：结构主义(主张“把意识拆成感觉元素再研究”)和行为主义(主张“心理不可研究，只研究刺激—反应”)，这2种都被格式塔派强烈反对。格式塔心理学是既反结构主义，又反行为主义的一种“第三条道路”。
text: German psychologist, one of the three founders of Gestalt psychology (Max Wertheimer, Wolfgang Kohler, Kurt Koffka)
The core focus of Gestalt psychology: perceptual integrity, psychological structure and overall laws

The background of the emergence of Gestalt psychology: the scientific revolution from the late 19th century to the early 20th century. The entire European academic community was shifting from traditional philosophical psychology to experimental-based scientific psychology. However, the "elementalism" that dominated the psychology community encountered a serious bottleneck.

Elementalism: All psychological activities can be decomposed into the smallest "elements" (similar to chemical elements). Perception = the simple sum of sensory elements. Psychology attempts to understand the mind through "splitting and decomposition" like natural science. Which creates a problem: Many psychological phenomena simply cannot be explained by “breaking it into smaller parts.”

The core viewpoint of Gestalt psychology: Based on reflection on the problem that "the whole cannot be explained by the sum of its parts", it is proposed that "the whole is greater than the sum of its parts"

The mainstream psychology circles at the time of its birth were: structuralism (which advocated "splitting consciousness into sensory elements and then studying them") and behaviorism (which advocated "psychology cannot be studied, only stimulus-response"), both of which were strongly opposed by the Gestaltists. Gestalt psychology is a "third way" that is both anti-structuralism and anti-behaviorism.

text: The ideological pioneer of Neoplatonism: Although Philo tried to use Platonic philosophy to explain Jewish classics, strictly speaking, he cannot be called a Neoplatonist.
He tried to combine Jewish religious beliefs with Greek philosophy, especially Platonism and Stoicism, pioneering "Hellenistic Judaism"
Use the concepts of Platonic philosophy to reinterpret the contents of the "Old Testament" as a Jewish classic, especially the "Genesis" in the "Old Testament"

God’s “Logos” or “idea” constitutes the origin of the world, while the perceptual world is just a copy of the “idea”. God created the world through “logos” or “idea”. This view laid an important theoretical foundation for the "incarnation" of Christianity, so Engels called Philo "the true father of Christianity."

Neoplatonism 1: Originated in the late Roman Empire around the 3rd century AD, represented by Plotinus, it was the most important systematic metaphysical development in ancient Western philosophy after Plato.

Neoplatonism 2: The ideological crisis in the late Roman Empire, with social unrest and political decline, people were dissatisfied with reality and turned to seek spiritual salvation and spiritual support. The need for philosophy shifted from rational inquiry to religious and mystical ultimate care.

Neoplatonism 3: The "integration needs" of the Greek philosophical system. The philosophical community at that time tried to integrate the ideas of Plato, Aristotle, the Stoics, and the Alexandrian School into a "grand unified system."

Neoplatonism 4: Religious environment - the impact of Greek religion, Eastern mysticism, Judeo-Christian thought, the rapid expansion of Judaism and early Christianity, posing challenges to traditional Greek philosophy. At that time, philosophers began to try to use "philosophical religion" and "religious philosophy" to respond to the needs of the times. Therefore, Neoplatonism has a strong sense of mystery, religion, and salvation.
Neoplatonism 5: The school of Alexandria systematized Plato's works and added religious interpretations.
Neoplatonism 6: "New" is reflected in the re-systematization, religiousization and metaphysics of Plato's thoughts.

Influence on Socrates and Plato: His moral criticism of Homer's mythology paved the way for Socrates and Plato to later criticize poetry and seek the divine "good".

History of theological thought: His view of the "only rational God" is regarded as the beginning of Greek rational theism and plays an ideological prototype role in the later Christian view of monotheism.
Pioneer of Skepticism: His distinction between "truth" and "opinion" makes him considered one of the early sources of skeptical thought in ancient Greece.
Modern philosophy: Hegel called him "the beginning of the transformation of thought from myth to rationality"
Modern scholars: It is generally believed that he is the founder of "philosophical theology" in the history of Western philosophy and an early pioneer of "epistemology"

source: 他在雅典的“彩绘柱廊”（Stoa Poikile）讲学，由此得名“斯多葛学派”（Stoic School）
芝诺以及早期斯多葛学派所关心的问题与伊壁鸠鲁主义相同，都是要探讨如何追求心灵的宁静
一个人要想获得幸福，就要顺应自然、服从命运，这才是一种道德的生活，而道德的生活就是幸福的生活
不要要求事情像你所希望的那样发生，而是接受实际发生的那样，控制我们对所发生的事情的态度，将会得到宁静和幸福
他一生淡泊名利，以清贫和理性生活著称，被雅典人视为“理性生活的典范”
text: He lectured in the Stoa Poikile in Athens, hence the name "Stoic School"
Zeno and the early Stoics were concerned with the same issues as Epicureanism: how to pursue peace of mind.
If a person wants to be happy, he must conform to nature and obey fate. This is a moral life, and a moral life is a happy life.
Don't ask for things to happen as you want them to happen, but accept them as they actually happen. Controlling our attitude towards what happens will lead to peace and happiness.
He was indifferent to fame and wealth throughout his life, and was known for his poverty and rational life. He was regarded by the Athenians as "a model of rational life."

source: 逻辑学：逻辑是理性思维的工具，真理来自与自然一致的理性判断
物理学：世界是一个有理性的整体，由“神圣理性（Logos）”支配，火是万物本原，宇宙循环(宇宙大火)
伦理学：顺应自然(理性)、服从命运，德性是唯一的善，保持心灵宁静
理性与自由：“只有睿智的人才是自由的，其他人都是奴隶。”
text: Logic: Logic is a tool for rational thinking. Truth comes from rational judgment consistent with nature.
Physics: The world is a rational whole, governed by "Divine Reason (Logos)", fire is the origin of all things, and the cycle of the universe (cosmic fire)
Ethics: Follow nature (rationality), obey fate, virtue is the only good, and keep the mind calm
Reason and freedom: "Only the wise are free, everyone else is a slave."

Roman thought: His ethical thoughts were introduced to Rome through the Stoic scholars in the middle period, and had a direct impact on Cicero, Seneca, Marcus Aurelius, etc.
Christian ethics: The concepts of "inherent virtue", "compliance with destiny" and "cosmic rationality" were absorbed by early Christianity into the concepts of God's will and rational laws
Modern Philosophy and Psychology: Zeno's view that "emotions arise from misjudgment" inspired the modern theory of **Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)**
